credits_cram.why: The paper calls CRAM an existing framework and a re-implementation, but never names Hoover, Blayney and Whittington or attributes the method to them.

cites_hoover.why: No \cite to a CRAM paper appears. The only citations are to other works (Shah, Saunshi, Feinashley, etc.), and CRAM is described without a citation.

small_n.why: "Direct solving was evaluated on 5 puzzles each for Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, and 10 puzzles for Haiku 5.5"; the paper calls the sample size ($N=5$ to $10$) a limitation.

handset_caveat.why: "an unlearned baseline with a single hand-set penalty weight achieves an identical 497/500 solved puzzles"; the results also compare 496--497 for learned energy against 497 for hand-set.

their_numbers.why: The 42 ms figure is labelled "reported on an NVIDIA H200 GPU in prior literature", separate from the authors' own 2.5 s CPU fit. The 99.996% figure is not used.

no_new_claims.why: It adds details absent from the log: 14 cores, 48GB, Clang 16, NumPy 1.26.4, Adam lr 0.01 with 150 epochs, beta=2.0, w0=1.0, a "$200" estimate, and failure-trace excerpts.
